question.prompt: A lattice point in an \(xy\)-coordinate system is any point \((x, y)\) where both \(x\) and \(y\) are integers. The graph of \(y=mx+2\) passes through no lattice point with \(0 \lt x \le 100\) for all \(m\) such that \(\dfrac{1}{2} \lt m \lt a.\) What is the maximum possible value of \(a?\)

solutions.explanation:
We need the smallest slope greater than \(1/2\) that makes the line pass through a lattice point in the specified strip.

If such a point has integer coordinates \((q,y)\), then \(1\le q\le100\), and the slope from \((0,2)\) to that point is
\[
m=\frac{y-2}{q}=\frac pq,
\]
where \(p=y-2\) is an integer. We seek the smallest possible \(p/q>1/2\). There is no need to require this fraction to be reduced.

If \(q\) is even, then \(q/2\) is an integer. Thus \(p>q/2\) requires \(p\ge q/2+1\), giving
\[
\frac pq\ge\frac12+\frac1q\ge\frac12+\frac1{100}.
\]
If \(q\) is odd, then the smallest integer above \(q/2\) is \((q+1)/2\). Since the largest allowed odd \(q\) is 99,
\[
\frac pq\ge\frac12+\frac1{2q}
\ge\frac12+\frac1{198}=\frac{50}{99}.
\]
The even-denominator bound is larger, because \(1/100>1/198\). The odd-denominator bound is attained by \(p=50\), \(q=99\), corresponding to the lattice point \((99,52)\).

Therefore every slope strictly between \(1/2\) and \(50/99\) avoids the specified lattice points. Taking \(a=50/99\) excludes the first forbidden slope because the condition is \(m<a\). Any larger \(a\) includes it and fails. The maximum is \(\boxed{50/99}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Find the first slope that reaches a lattice point
